why: RC-04. tools/run_negative_fixtures.py had no denominator: with 1 of 27 fixtures present it printed `negative_fixtures_rejected: 1` and exited 0, and validate_contracts.py accepted that as its negative control. The only guards were `if not fixtures` and `fixtures > 0`, which catch the empty directory and nothing else. This file is the declared count, and it is hand-maintained on purpose: a denominator derived from the directory it measures cannot notice a deletion. Adding a fixture means adding its id here; removing one means removing it here, which is a line in a diff a reviewer sees.
checked_by: tools/run_negative_fixtures.py: declared-but-absent and present-but-undeclared both fail
validate_contracts.py: the fixture run's own count must equal this one, and every declared fixture must have been rejected
floor_why: RC4-03. A literal, for the reason every other floor in this package is a literal: a count derived from the file it measures is satisfied by the empty file. RC-04 gave this suite a DECLARED denominator, which catches a fixture deleted from the tree alone; it did not catch a fixture deleted from the tree AND from this list in one edit, because one hand writes both. Measured by the fourth recheck: 34 of 36 fixtures moved out of the directory and struck from this list together, full run exit 0, `checks: 288620` -- byte-identical to the baseline and to every conjunct_walk field -- with `negative_fixtures_rejected: 2`. Nothing compared that 2 to anything. It matters here more than anywhere: the only control that catches a mutation of the demand table is a fixture in this list. validate_contracts.py carries the same number as a literal and compares the two, so lowering it takes two edits a reviewer sees, and the reason goes in the constant's comment there. RAISED BY R18 (the Step 6 repair of the F2 layer): negative 56 -> 91, positive 17 -> 52. Thirty-five new adverse cases and thirty-five paired benign ones, one per finding the four Step 6 reviews raised against the contracts, plus one pair per guard that had none. F6C-16 measured 14 of 30 guards exercised by a paired fixture; every registered guard has one now, and the count is derived rather than quoted -- `comm -12 <(grep -rhoE 'guard\.[a-z0-9_.]+' fixtures/negative | sort -u) <(grep -rhoE 'guard\.[a-z0-9_.]+' fixtures/positive | sort -u) | wc -l`. Lowering either number is still two edits and a written reason. RAISED TO THE COMMITTED COUNT BY THE RC5 REPAIR: negative 92 -> 94 (RC5-01, RC5-03: the allowlist-literal pair and the not-admitted pair) and 94 -> 95 (RC5-02: the pin-coverage pair). R20 (F6A-10): 95 -> 96, the closed-enum membership pair. R21 (F6D-12): 96 -> 97, the seventh-reason pair. R22 (F6D-09): 97 -> 98, the predicate-bearing type pair. R23 (F6C-11): 98 -> 99, the retention-comparison pair. R24 (F6C-10): 99 -> 100, the attempt-ceiling pair. R25 (F6D-09, the wrong_reason repair): 100 -> 101, the predicate-implementation-status pair. The F6D-09 tripwire had to stop firing on the negative-fixture sentinel, because a fixture that adds a predicate must give that predicate a status and was tripping a check about the CONTRACT's classification inside its own scratch tree -- which is what refused r3-lifecycle-status-as-judgment-subject for a reason it was not written for. The pair is what bounds the exclusion: the adverse case gives a real predicate a real second classification and the tripwire must still fire; the benign case gives one the sentinel and it must not.
